newsitem.title: USA: N.Y Pataki hopes to approve school reforms on Tues.
newsitem.headline: N.Y Pataki hopes to approve school reforms on Tues.

text.p: New York State Gov. George Pataki on Monday said that he hoped the special legislative session that he called to begin on Tuesday will approve school governance for New York City on the same day.
"There are still some minor differences among the parties, but nothing that I think should stand in the way of being able to pass the bill tomorrow," he told reporters in Albany.

While the governor did not disclose what the differences over school reform were, he also held out to New York City the possibility that its personal income tax surcharge, which expires at year-end, would be extended for more than one year.

"I would hope that we could give the city the assurance that the Personal Income Tax extender will go on for a number of years so they can budget accordingly." The tax helps pay for the city's police, and the Giuliani Administration wants it extended for four years.
The special legislative session also is expected to extend a Metropolitan Transportation Authority tax for 12 downstate counties.
